clue.text: Lady R may suggest an isolated place

parts.note: these words are RYDAL spelt from the end, so they are Rydal Water read backwards; Rydal Water is a small lake in England's Lake District

explanation.surface: A titled woman known only by an initial is said to hint at somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady R' looks like a person, but it is RYDAL written backwards, and Rydal Water is a lake in Cumbria. So 'Lady R' is that water turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiet spot cut off from the main current of events, like a stagnant side-channel of a river, is called this.

clue.text: Unpleasant sign when stomach initially turns over

indicators.note: the opening pair of letters of the stomach word is flipped, so only the start is turned round

parts.note: the abdomen is the belly or stomach region

explanation.surface: A queasy lurch in the gut is taken as a warning of trouble ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially turns over' swaps just the first two letters of ABDOMEN, so the A moves behind the B.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent; an ill one is an unpleasant sign of things to come.

clue.text: Eggs the Bard said wasted on the general

definitions.text: Eggs the Bard said wasted on the general

parts.words: Eggs the Bard said wasted on the general
parts.note: in Hamlet a play that pleased not the million is called a fine delicacy 'to the general', meaning lost on the general public; sturgeon roe is the eggs

explanation.surface: Shakespeare remarks that some fine eggs were thrown away on an army commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the general' is not a military officer but the general public, as in Hamlet's line; the old spelling with a final E is the one Shakespeare used.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeon roe is a luxury food made of salted fish eggs, and the Hamlet phrase means something too refined for ordinary taste.

clue.text: Campaign of intimidation was forever struggling to encompass the end of Putin

indicators.note: to encompass means the jumbled letters surround the next piece
struggling suggests the letters of the two words writhing into a new order
the end of picks the final letter of the leader's surname

explanation.surface: The Russian president is caught up in a long-running battle of nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges WASFOREVER, and 'to encompass' puts N, the last letter of Putin, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sustained effort to unsettle an opponent through threats and pressure rather than open fighting goes by this name.

clue.text: Child seat arranged for As You Like It

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of seat are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A child's seat is set out for a performance of the Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles SEAT into ASTE. The play title is the definition, read as an instruction 'as you like it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipes say add salt to suit your own preference, which is the same as however you like it.

clue.text: Animal wheeling to take exact position between two groups of soldiers retreating

indicators.note: retreating means the whole assembly is read backwards, as troops fall back
between means the fitting word sits in the middle of the two army groups

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers and OR is other ranks, two bodies of British soldiers
to fit is to sit exactly in place

explanation.surface: An animal circles round to occupy a precise spot between two withdrawing army units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts FIT between RE and OR, giving REFITOR, and 'retreating' turns that round. 'wheeling' belongs to the definition: these creatures are called wheel animals.
explanation.definitionFit: These microscopic water creatures have a crown of beating hairs that looks like a turning wheel.

clue.text: Fraudster may be seen by senior policeman as excellent

definitions.text: may be seen by senior policeman as excellent
definitions.meaning: a superintendent is a super, and super-... means excellent, so this word follows the super

explanation.definitionFit: One who dupes is a cheat or swindler, and the word also completes the rhyming phrase meaning first-rate after the police rank.

clue.text: American litigant in one of several ministries initially

definitions.meaning: John ... is the name US courts give an unnamed party in a lawsuit
the initials of a Department of Energy or Department of the Environment

explanation.definitionFit: US courts name an anonymous party John Doe, and the initials also abbreviate British and American government departments of Energy or Environment.

clue.text: Calm at opening position

indicators.note: opening means the small word goes into and splits open the word for position

parts.note: a place is a position

explanation.surface: Someone stays composed at the start of a race or game position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' is a container signal here: the small word is put into the position word, not placed at its start.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm someone angry is to pacify or appease them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Enters race without water and becomes exhausted

parts.note: someone who enters a race runs in it
dry means lacking water

explanation.surface: An athlete takes part in a race with nothing to drink and flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply that is used up, like a well or funds, is said to have dried up completely.

clue.text: Reviled footballer may be Olympic medallist

definitions.meaning: a player who falls over to fake a foul is scorned as a ...
a competitor who plunges from a board, as in Olympic diving events

explanation.surface: A much-hated football player turns out to have won a medal at the Games.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is both a player who feigns being fouled and a springboard or platform athlete.

clue.text: Storehouse once 10% full?

parts.note: a tithe was the tenth of a crop paid to the church, and it was kept in a big farm building, so the store held a tenth

explanation.surface: A storage building that used to be only a tenth full.
explanation.walkthrough: '10% full' sounds like a nearly empty barn, but it means a building full of the church's one-tenth share.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval parishes stored the tenth of each harvest owed to the church in a large dedicated farm building.

clue.text: Endless complaint from one unable to fly

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the grumble is cut off

parts.note: a moan is a complaint

explanation.surface: A never-ending grumble comes from someone who cannot take to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: This extinct giant bird of New Zealand was flightless, like the ostrich and emu.

clue.text: Athletic striker to move on without playing

parts.note: athletic in the sense of quick-moving, fast
in football a striker is a forward

explanation.surface: A sporty attacker moves on to the next club without getting a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the definition is skipping through a recording without playing it.
explanation.definitionFit: On a tape or video player, this button winds onward quickly past content without playing it.

clue.text: Doctor Arnold hides in state

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician named Arnold is hiding somewhere in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the anagram signal, rearranging ARNOLDHIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest of the fifty US states lies in New England.

clue.text: Africans' leaders in no doubt even Britain expects little else

indicators.note: leaders means the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: The heads of African nations are sure Britain wants little more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first letter of each word from 'no' to 'else'; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ndebele are a southern African people living chiefly in Zimbabwe and South Africa.

clue.text: Castle nearly losing odd bits in overcrowded area

parts.note: in chess the castle is the rook

indicators.note: losing odd bits means the first, third and fifth letters of nearly go, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A castle almost loses some strange pieces in a crowded district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing odd bits' keeps the even letters of 'nearly', ERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum packed with people is likened to a breeding colony of crows, crammed with nests.

clue.text: No end of fruit in pub for Simon

indicators.note: in means the shortened fruit goes inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter of the fruit is dropped

parts.note: an olive is a fruit

explanation.surface: A pub offers endless fruit to a man called Simon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simon' looks like any man's name, but it points to Simón Bolívar, the liberator of much of South America; 'No end of' and 'in' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Simón Bolívar was the South American liberator, so Simon is his first name.

clue.text: To be obliged to open sack was good

indicators.note: to open means the obligation word goes into the bed word, splitting it

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
to have to do something is to be obliged to do it

explanation.surface: Someone forced to open a sack turned out to have done well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to open' is a container signal; 'sack' is the slang word for bed, as in hitting the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who behaved acted properly, so the verb means conducted oneself well.

clue.text: Make fun of Frenchman opening part of race naked?

indicators.note: opening means the Frenchman goes into the race piece

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a race
M is short for monsieur, a Frenchman
naked is nothing on: O for nothing, then ON

explanation.surface: A Frenchman starts one leg of a race with no clothes on, inviting ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' puts M inside LAP. 'naked' is read as 'nothing on', O plus ON, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise someone is to mock them in a ridiculing piece of writing or speech.

clue.text: Fake news in salesman's returns

indicators.note: in means the untruth goes inside the salesman word

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative; with the S it gives REPS
fake news is a lie

explanation.surface: A salesman's figures are boosted by false reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'returns' looks like goods sent back, but it means answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Retorts and responses are what someone gives back when spoken to.

clue.text: Letter read out succeeded after repeat, which you can bet on

indicators.note: after means the succeeded letter comes behind the doubled piece
repeat means the spoken letter appears twice in a row

parts.note: the letter G is spoken as 'gee'
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A letter is read aloud again and again, and the punters place their wagers.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken name of G, written GEE, is doubled, and S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: In British baby talk gee-gees are horses, which punters back at racecourses.

clue.text: Having lost weight after golf, one picks up

indicators.note: after means the slimmer word follows the single letter

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
one who has slimmed down is leaner

explanation.surface: A golfer who has slimmed down picks things up from the course.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner gathers leftover grain after harvest, collecting what others missed.

clue.text: Account for one dumped on prairie

indicators.note: on means in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a former partner who has been dropped is an ex
a prairie is a flat grassy plain

explanation.surface: Someone must justify why a jilted lover was abandoned on the grasslands.
explanation.definitionFit: To give reasons for something is to make it clear, to give the reasons behind it.

clue.text: Resilient, like May, could one say?

definitions.meaning: May falls in spring, so something like May might jokingly be called spring-like with a Y ending

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether May could be described as bouncing back.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means elastic and bouncy, and humorously also of the season containing May.

clue.text: We move home with passion

indicators.note: move means the letters of the two words are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: We relocate house with great enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges HOMEPASSION; 'with' is a link and 'We' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans as a species are the speakers of the clue, so the scientific name of mankind stands for we.

clue.text: Piece trimmed is level

indicators.note: trimmed means the last letter of the piece word is cut off

parts.note: a part is a piece

explanation.surface: A trimmed piece of wood is now flat and even.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a par means being equal, as in level pegging.

clue.text: Old instrument people, snapping head off, abuse

parts.note: the viol is an old stringed instrument

indicators.note: snapping head off means the first letter of the people word is broken away

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: People snapping the head off an old instrument is plain mistreatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach of rights or an assault is a violation, as is mistreating a rule.

clue.text: From girl, a cry of surprise

parts.note: 'my!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A girl lets out a cry of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's given name, as in the novelist Amy Tan.

clue.text: A fellow seizes one violently

indicators.note: seizes means the fellow word grips the numeral inside it

parts.note: a fellow is a man
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man grabs someone else with brute force.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning with full force, as in sailors heaving vehemently.

clue.text: Hard to leave boat looking shabby

indicators.note: to leave means the hard letter goes out of the boat word

parts.note: a dinghy is a small boat
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: It is tough to abandon a boat that has become shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimy and drab in appearance, dull and dirty from neglect.

clue.text: Harshness of way to travel about in state in America

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to ride is to travel

indicators.note: in means the about letter sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York, a US state
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone complains of the roughness of journeying around a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives the letter for circa rather than signalling a reversal, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating, shrill quality of sound or tone is a kind of harshness.
